newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee ends at day's lows, Jan below $1,400.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee ends at day's lows, Jan below $1,400.

text.p: London's robusta coffee futures resumed their slide in the afternoon to end sharply down on long liquidation, traders said.
Benchmark January dipped to finish at below $1,400 a tonne for the first time since November 4 when it closed at $1,389.
By the finish, the second-month position stood $16 down at $1,390, the day's low, after triggering some sell-stops earlier in the day at just below $1,400.
Traders said the January contract could now find some support at around $1,360.
Traders said some disappointed longs liquidated their positions amid a drought of market-moving news.
"The (U.S.) stock figures have little difference on the market," said a trader. "For the time being, the market is technically driven."
Exchange volume was 5,514 lots, with January and March accounting for about half of the turnover.
The Jan/March switch was quite active, trading at $45-$46 as players rolled forward their nearby positions.
Activity is expected to slow down for the rest of the week due to the Thanksgiving holiday in New York on Thursday and Friday.
Front-month November's premium to January shrank further ahead of the contract's expiry on Friday to $35 at the close from $54 on Tuesday.
"We're are going to have a few kamikaze spreads in the next few days but you can safely say that 95 percent of the people have got out of November," said one trader.
The London market basically brushed aside a spate of fundamental news, traders said.
In Vietnam, local traders warned of mould problems if rains kept pounding the crop while Nicaragua reported serious transport problems.
In Brazil, many of the country's ports faced their second day of a strike but two of those contacted by Reuters had either returned to work on Wednesday or had not stopped operations on Tuesday.
Traders doubt if the strike would be prolonged. "Many of the workers are daily- or weekly-rated," said one.
